claims.text: Premelting and melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the interplay of grain-boundary energy, atomic-level lattice distortion, surface effects, and internal defects.
The proposed material system includes CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
The proposed particle-diameter range is 5-50 nm.
Particle size, composition, and surface coating will be varied while the synthesis method is held constant.
Testing will be conducted from 300 to 1000 K at a heating rate of 5 K/min under an inert atmosphere.
Smaller high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have higher grain-boundary energy.
Smaller high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have increased lattice distortion.
Higher grain-boundary energy lowers the melting point of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Increased lattice distortion lowers the melting point of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Higher grain-boundary energy produces more pronounced premelting behavior.
Increased lattice distortion produces more pronounced premelting behavior.
Surface effects modify lattice distortions and the energy landscape of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Internal defects modify lattice distortions and the energy landscape of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Changes in surface coating alter the melting and premelting behavior.
Changes in internal-defect density alter the melting and premelting behavior.
Decreasing particle size will systematically decrease melting point.
Decreasing particle size will systematically increase premelting behavior.
DSC and XRD can reveal the predicted changes in melting point and premelting behavior.
A failure of melting point and premelting behavior to vary systematically with particle size, composition, and surface coating would falsify the hypothesis.
